messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Hindi, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Hindi line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
और फिर तुम उन लोगों को देखोगे जो संतुष्ट हैं आग में क्योंकि वे आने की आशा रखते हैं, जब भी वह धन्य लोगों के पास हो।

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Word Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word / Phrase | Back‑Translation | Status | |-------------|----------------------|----------------------|------------------|--------| | e | coordinating conjunction introducing a new clause | और फिर | “and then” | OK | | vederai | future 2nd sg. of *vedere* – “you will see” | देखोगे | “you will see” | OK | | color | demonstrative pronoun referring to a group – “those” | उन लोगों | “those people” | OK | | che | relative pronoun – “who/that” | जो | “who/that” | OK | | son | present 3rd pl. of *essere* – “are” | हैं | “are” | OK | | contenti | predicative adjective – “contented” | संतुष्ट | “contented” | OK | | nel | preposition “in” + article – locative | में | “in” | OK | | foco | noun “fire” | आग | “fire” | OK | | perché | causal conjunction – “because” | क्योंकि | “because” | OK | | speran | present 3rd pl. of *sperare* – “they hope” | रखते हैं | “they hope” | OK | | di | preposition introducing infinitive – “to” | की | “of / for” (marks infinitive) | OK | | venire | infinitive “to come” | आने | “to come” | OK | | quando | temporal adverb – “whenever/when” | जब | “when” | OK | | che* (idiomatic particle in *quando che*) | reinforces temporal clause, no lexical meaning | भी | “ever” (as in “whenever”) | OK | | sia | present subjunctive of *essere* – “may be” | हो | “may be” | OK | | a | preposition of direction – “to” | के | “to / of” (as part of “के पास”) | OK | | le | definite article, feminine plural – “the” (not required in Hindi) | — (omitted) | — | UNNECESSARY | | beate | adjective “blessed” | धन्य | “blessed” | OK | | genti | noun “folk/people” | लोगों | “people” | OK |
\*The particle **che** in *quando che* has no independent lexical content; it is rendered by the Hindi particle **भी** to preserve the “whenever” sense.
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: **le** – Hindi does not use definite articles, so the word is omitted in the translation. No other source tokens are missing or incorrectly rendered.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Hindi script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Hindi text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- Line 118: - Original: और फिर तुम उन लोगों को देखोगे जो संतुष्ट हैं - Issue: none - Corrected: और फिर तुम उन लोगों को देखोगे जो संतुष्ट हैं - Line 119: - Original: आग में क्योंकि वे आने की आशा रखते हैं, - Issue: none - Corrected: आग में क्योंकि वे आने की आशा रखते हैं, - Line 120: - Original: जब भी वह धन्य लोगों के पास हो। - Issue: none - Corrected: जब भी वह धन्य लोगों के पास हो।
